title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 123
paragraphs: Similarly, the Alcmaeonidae were haters of tyrants to the same degree as he, or more. So it is a matter of wonder to me, and I do not accept the charge that they were the ones who displayed the shield — seeing that throughout the entire time of the tyranny they were in exile, and that it was by their contrivance that the sons of Pisistratus were made to give up their rule. They, to my judgment, did far more to set Athens free than Harmodius and Aristogiton. For those two, by killing Hipparchus, only enraged the rest of the house of Pisistratus and did not cause the others to stop their tyranny; whereas the Alcmaeonidae manifestly freed Athens — at least if it is true, as I have set forth before, that they were the ones who persuaded the Pythian prophetess to instruct the Lacedaemonians to set Athens free.
